instructions_en: Please indicate for each of the five statements which is closest to how you have been feeling over the last two weeks. Notice that higher numbers mean better well-being. Example: If you have felt cheerful and in good spirits more than half of the time during the last two weeks, select number three.
instructions_ko: 다음 다섯 문장 각각에 대해, 지난 2주 동안 내가 느낀 것과 가장 가까운 것을 고르세요. 숫자가 높을수록 정신적 안녕 상태가 좋다는 뜻입니다. 예: 지난 2주 중 절반 이상의 기간 동안 즐겁고 기분이 좋았다면 3을 고르세요.

labels_en: Less than half of the time
More than half of the time

items.en: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits
I have felt calm and relaxed
I have felt active and vigorous
I woke up feeling fresh and rested
items.ko: 나는 아침에 상쾌하고 푹 쉰 느낌으로 잠에서 깼다.

items.en: My daily life has been filled with things that interest me
items.ko: 나의 일상은 내가 흥미를 느끼는 일들로 채워져 있었다.

scoring.total: raw = sum of 5 items (0-25); percentage = raw x 4 (0-100). 0 = worst, 100 = best possible mental well-being.
scoring.cutoff: Percentage below 50 (raw below 13) has been suggested as a cut-off for poor mental well-being and as an indication for further assessment (WHO 2024, citing Topp et al., 2015). Screening signal only, not a diagnosis.

notes: English items, 0-5 anchors, time frame, instructions, scoring and licence read from the WHO 2024 PDF (WHO/UCN/MSD/MHE/2024.1).
English item text has no final period in the WHO form; kept as printed.
No Korean version on the WHO page (26 other languages listed) nor on the archived Psychiatric Centre North Zealand translation list (no Korean).

A Korean WHO-5 was used in Kim HJ et al. (2010), J Korean Geriatr Psychiatry 14(2):90-96, but its wording was not publicly accessible; all Korean text here (items, anchors, instructions) is self-translated and unverified.
